heading: What Are Automation Used
content:
Yes, I've done some automation using shell scripting, mainly to handle
space issues.

We built automation to move files from the data directory to the archive
directory --- specifically files older than 2 weeks. So anything older
than 2 weeks automatically gets moved into archive.

Then, after 8 months, those archived files get moved further into a
backup server using SFTP, in a zipped format.

For this, I used shell scripting --- I used the find command to identify
log files older than 14 days, then used the tar command to compress
them, moved them into the archive directory, and used SFTP to send them
to the remote server.

I scheduled this whole thing through crontab, to run every day at 11
o'clock --- that's 0 11

heading: Automation 2
content:
I also built another automation to send a report of long-running jobs
through email.

We collect long-running jobs using the top command and ps -ef, and from
that we identify processes that have been running for more than 3 days.
We take those process names and send them out in a mail to our internal
team.

Ps basically stands for process --- it's like Task Manager in Windows.
If I just run ps without any options, it shows me the processes running
in the current terminal.

If I run ps -ef, it lists everything, and every process has its own
process ID.

For this automation, I used ps -ef along with the top command, and
there's a utility called mailx in Unix that I used to actually send out
the emails.

I combined mailx with the ps -ef and top output to send this list to the
distribution list, and scheduled the whole thing through crontab.
